# Slabstones Rearrangement

Problem PE
Slabstones Rearrangement
Time limit: 3 seconds
Memory limit: 1024 megabytes
Problem Description
Babara has a garden. She has bought some rectangular slabstones and worked out an initial
placement of all slabstones in the garden. The shape of the garden is rectangular. An edge
of a slabstone should be either parallel or orthogonal to an edge of the garden. There exists a
slabstone touching the left, right, bottom, and top edges of the garden, respectively. All the
slabstones are contained in the garden. Meanwhile, none of the slabstones overlap in the initial
placement. Babara enjoys stepping slabstones from one to another every day. However, Babara
would like to redesign her garden to make room for some other purposes. She is wondering how
tight the slabstones can be packed together if they can only be shifted horizontally (i.e., left
or right) without changing their vertical coordinates. Furthermore, if the vertical dimensions
of any two slabstones overlap (not including touching of their ends), their relative locations in
the horizontal direction should be maintained. That is, if the vertical dimensions of slabstones
R and Q overlap and, before shifting, slabstone Q is on the right of slabstone R, Q should be
still on the right of R after shifting or vice versa. Besides, there is a minimal horizontal spacing
between two slabstones during slabstone rearrangement if their vertical dimensions overlap.
The slabstones should remain non-overlapping after shifting. Nevertheless, their horizontal
edges may touch. Now you are asked to help Babara calculate the largest area that can be
spared for other purposes.
Input Format
The first line holds an integer specifying the number of test cases. It is then followed by the
input data of the test cases. The first line of the input for each test case gives two integers.
The first one specifies the number of rectangular slabstones whereas the second one gives the
minimal horizontal spacing between two slabstones. Then, each of the following lines contains
four integers. The first two integers specify the initial x and y coordinates of the bottom-left
corner of a slabstone in the garden. The remaining two integers specify the initial x and y
coordinates of the top-right corner of a slabstone. Two adjacent numbers are separated by a
whitespace.
Output Format
The output of a test case takes a line. It contains the largest area saved by shifting the
slabstones. If no area can be saved, just output zero.
1

Technical Specification
 The number of test cases is not more than 32.
 All the coordinates are 32-bit unsigned integers.
 A garden’s area is not larger than the maximal 32-bit unsigned integer.
 The width and length of a slabstone are 32-bit unsigned integers. They should be larger
than zero.
 The minimal horizontal spacing between any two slabstones is a 32-bit unsigned integer
and should be greater than zero.
 The number of slabstones is from 4 to 100.
Sample Input 1
2
4 2
2 6 4 12
8 4 16 8
7 10 11 16
18 4 20 18
6 4
2 5 4 11
2 14 6 17
7 10 10 16
9 4 16 7
11 11 16 14
18 4 20 18
Sample Output 1
28
0
2

[PDF](https://codeforces.com/gym/105544/attachments/download/28405/2023-taiwan.pdf)

# Slabstones Rearrangement

Time limit: 3 seconds. Memory limit: 1024 megabytes.

## Problem Description

Babara has a rectangular garden containing rectangular slabstones. Every slabstone lies inside the garden, and its sides are parallel to the garden's sides. The slabstones do not overlap. Each of the four sides of the garden is touched by at least one slabstone.

Babara wants to rearrange the slabstones to reduce the area of the garden. A slabstone can only move horizontally: its vertical position cannot change. The slabstones must remain non-overlapping. For any two slabstones whose vertical projections overlap with positive length, their left-to-right order must remain unchanged and their horizontal separation must be at least the given positive minimum spacing. The horizontal edges of slabstones may touch.

Find the maximum area that can be freed by this rearrangement. If no area can be freed, output zero.

## Input Format

The first line contains the number of test cases $T$.

For each test case, the first line contains the number of slabstones $n$ and the required minimum spacing. Each of the next $n$ lines contains four integers $x_1,y_1,x_2,y_2$, the coordinates of the lower-left and upper-right corners of a slabstone, respectively.

## Output Format

For each test case, output the maximum area that can be freed, or zero if the garden's area cannot be reduced.

## Technical Specification

- $1\le T\le32$ and $4\le n\le100$.
- All coordinates are unsigned 32-bit integers.
- The original garden's area does not exceed the maximum unsigned 32-bit integer.
- The width and height of each slabstone and the minimum spacing are positive unsigned 32-bit integers.


## Sample 1

### Input

```text
2
4 2
2 6 4 12
8 4 16 8
7 10 11 16
18 4 20 18
6 4
2 5 4 11
2 14 6 17
7 10 10 16
9 4 16 7
11 11 16 14
18 4 20 18
```

### Output

```text
28
0
```

translation.markdown:
# 石板重排

时间限制：3 秒。内存限制：1024 MB。

## 题目描述

Babara 有一座放着若干矩形石板的矩形花园。所有石板都位于花园内，边与花园的边平行，且彼此不重叠。花园的四条边各自都至少与一块石板接触。

Babara 想通过重新排列石板缩小花园的面积。石板只能水平移动，竖直位置不能改变。移动后，石板仍不能重叠。对于竖直投影有正长度重叠的任意两块石板，它们的左右顺序不能改变，且水平方向的间距必须至少达到给定的正数最小间距。石板的水平边可以相接触。

求重新排列后最多可以腾出多少面积。如果不能腾出任何面积，输出零。

## 输入格式

第一行包含测试用例数 $T$。

对于每个测试用例，第一行包含石板数 $n$ 和要求的最小间距。接下来 $n$ 行，每行包含四个整数 $x_1,y_1,x_2,y_2$，依次表示一块石板左下角和右上角的坐标。

## 输出格式

对于每个测试用例，输出最多可以腾出的面积。如果花园面积不能减小，则输出零。

## 数据范围

- $1\le T\le32$，且 $4\le n\le100$。
- 所有坐标均为 32 位无符号整数。
- 原花园面积不超过 32 位无符号整数的最大值。
- 每块石板的宽、高以及要求的最小间距均为正的 32 位无符号整数。


## 样例 1

### 输入

```text
2
4 2
2 6 4 12
8 4 16 8
7 10 11 16
18 4 20 18
6 4
2 5 4 11
2 14 6 17
7 10 10 16
9 4 16 7
11 11 16 14
18 4 20 18
```

### 输出

```text
28
0
```
